Estimate ancestry proportions with the ADMIXTURE method

Source: R/gt_radmix.R
gt_radmix.Rd

This function estimates individual ancestry proportions (Q) and the allele frequencies of the ancestral populations (P) with the method of ADMIXTURE (Alexander et al. 2009), i.e. by maximum likelihood under the ADMIXTURE model. It uses the optimisation strategy of ADMIXTURE: a few EM iterations to prime a random start, then block-wise Newton updates of Q and P, each solved as a constrained quadratic program, accelerated by the quasi-Newton scheme of Zhou, Alexander and Lange (2011). It also offers the cross-validation of ADMIXTURE to choose K (Alexander and Lange 2011), a start from a truncated singular value decomposition (SVD) of the genotypes, supervised analyses with individuals of known ancestry, and support for pseudohaploid data. With genotype likelihoods (given by another package, see gt_radmix_data()), it fits the model of NGSadmix (Skotte et al. 2013), the ADMIXTURE model for low-depth sequencing data, with the same algorithm. If you use this function, please cite Alexander et al. (2009) for the method, and, if you use cross-validation, Alexander and Lange (2011); with genotype likelihoods, also cite Skotte et al. (2013).

Usage

gt_radmix(
  x,
  k,
  n_runs = 1,
  seed = NULL,
  max_iter = 1000,
  rtol = 1e-08,
  n_em_iter = 5,
  n_qn = 3,
  init = c("random", "svd"),
  svd_power = 3,
  init_q = NULL,
  init_p = NULL,
  fix_q = FALSE,
  fix_p = FALSE,
  supervised = NULL,
  use_imputed = FALSE,
  crossval = FALSE,
  n_folds = 5,
  cv_max_iter = max_iter,
  cv_rtol = max(rtol, 1e-07),
  n_cores = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

a tidypopgen::gen_tibble, or genotype likelihoods from another package (see "Genotype likelihoods" in the details), possibly grouped

k

an integer vector giving the number(s) of ancestral populations

n_runs

the number of runs for each value of k (defaults to 1)

seed

the seed for the random number generator (defaults to NULL). Either a vector of length n_runs (the same seeds are used for each k) or of length n_runs * length(k). The global random number generator state is restored on exit.

max_iter

the maximum number of iterations (defaults to 1000)

rtol

the convergence threshold on the relative change in log-likelihood between iterations (defaults to 1e-8). A threshold of 1e-7 takes 10-20% less time, but can stop a few log-likelihood units short of convergence, with ancestry proportions up to about 0.05 away from the converged ones

n_em_iter

the number of EM iterations used to prime the estimates (defaults to 5, as in ADMIXTURE); not used with init = "svd"

n_qn

the number of secant pairs used by the quasi-Newton acceleration (defaults to 3, as in ADMIXTURE)

init

how the starting values of each run are chosen: "random" (the default), random values followed by n_em_iter EM iterations, as in ADMIXTURE; or "svd", from a truncated SVD of the genotypes, which needs fewer iterations but is not suited to exploring the modes of the likelihood with several runs (see "Starting values from the SVD" in the details). "svd" cannot be combined with init_q or init_p.

svd_power

the number of power iterations of the randomised SVD of genotype likelihoods used by init = "svd" (defaults to 3; see "Starting values from the SVD" in the details). Not used with genotypes, whose truncated SVD is computed by tidypopgen::gt_pca_partialSVD()

init_q

optional matrix (individuals x k) of starting ancestry proportions; only allowed with a single value of k

init_p

optional matrix (loci x k) of starting allele frequencies (of the alternate allele, or of allele2 for genotype likelihoods, as in the P matrices returned by this function; those of tidypopgen::gt_admixture() give the frequency of the reference allele, so use 1 - P); only allowed with a single value of k. If it has row names (as the P matrices returned by this function), they are used to match its rows to the loci of x (it can then include other loci, which are ignored); otherwise its rows must be in the order of the loci of x

fix_q, fix_p

booleans; if TRUE, Q (respectively P) is kept at the value given in init_q (respectively init_p)

supervised

optional vector (character or factor) with one element per individual of x, for a supervised analysis (as ADMIXTURE's --supervised): the population of each reference individual, whose ancestry is then fixed, and NA for the individuals to estimate. k must be a single value, equal to the number of populations. See "Supervised analyses" in the details.

use_imputed

boolean; if TRUE, imputed genotypes are used as if they were observed; otherwise they are treated as missing (the default). Only for genotypes.

crossval

boolean; should the cross-validation error be computed (defaults to FALSE)? See the details. Only for genotypes.

n_folds

the number of folds used for cross-validation (defaults to 5, as in ADMIXTURE)

cv_max_iter, cv_rtol

the maximum number of iterations and the convergence threshold of the refit of each fold in cross-validation (default to max_iter, as for the full data, and to 1e-7, or rtol if it is larger). Smaller cv_max_iter or larger cv_rtol make cross-validation faster but bias its errors downwards (see "Cross-validation" in the details).

n_cores

the number of cores to use (defaults to 1); the results do not depend on it

verbose

boolean; should progress be printed (defaults to FALSE)? With verbose = TRUE, the log-likelihood is also computed (and logged) every 5 EM steps during the initial EM iterations; otherwise only their number is logged, as these values are not needed by the algorithm.

Value

an object of class gt_admix, a list with elements:

  • k the number of clusters of each run

  • Q a list of tidypopgen::q_matrix() objects with the ancestry proportions

  • P a list of matrices (loci x k) with the alternate allele frequencies (frequencies of allele2 for genotype likelihoods)

  • log a list with the log of each run

  • loglik the log-likelihood of each run

  • converged whether each run converged

  • cv the cross-validation error of each run (if crossval is TRUE)

  • id the id column of x

  • group the group column of x (if x is grouped)

  • ref_pops the reference population of each column of Q and P (only for a supervised analysis)

  • algorithm "radmix"

Details

Genotypes are read directly from the backing file of the gen_tibble (respecting any filtering of individuals and selection of loci), so no intermediate PLINK file is written; the same holds for genotype likelihoods, which the package that stores them gives to gt_radmix() through a method of gt_radmix_data(). Computation is in C++, multithreaded with OpenMP. The C++ code started as a port of the Julia package OpenADMIXTURE.jl (Ko et al. 2023), and has since been extensively rewritten; its solver of the quadratic programs, its projections, its quasi-Newton step and the structure of its fitting loop are still derived from OpenADMIXTURE.jl, and the alternating least squares of init = "svd" are adapted from ADAMIXTURE (see the file COPYRIGHTS of the package, system.file("COPYRIGHTS", package = "tidygenclust")).

Missing genotypes are ignored in the likelihood. Pseudohaploid individuals (see tidypopgen::gt_pseudohaploid()) contribute a single allele per locus. Only diploid and pseudohaploid gen_tibbles are supported.

P gives the frequency of the alternate allele (allele_alt in tidypopgen::show_loci()) in each ancestral population (for genotype likelihoods, of allele2, often the minor allele; see "Genotype likelihoods" below).

Supplying init_p together with fix_p = TRUE estimates the ancestry of new individuals given the allele frequencies of a reference panel (a "projection" analysis); the loci of x must then match the rows of init_p.

Algorithm

As in ADMIXTURE (Alexander et al. 2009; Alexander and Lange 2011), each run consists of:

  1. a random initialisation followed by a few EM iterations (n_em_iter; the EM algorithm of FRAPPE, Tang et al. 2005), or, with init = "svd", a start from the SVD of the genotypes (see below);

  2. block-wise Newton updates (block relaxation): all of Q given P (one individual at a time, on the simplex), then all of P given the new Q (one locus at a time, in the unit interval). Each Newton step is solved exactly as a small quadratic program, by an active-set method based on the sweep operator (Lange 2010);

  3. quasi-Newton acceleration (Zhou, Alexander and Lange 2011): each iteration applies two rounds of block updates, and the changes that they made in the last n_qn iterations (secant pairs) give a quasi-Newton step, which is accepted only when it improves the log-likelihood of the previous iteration (otherwise the iteration ends with the plain block updates).

Iterations stop when the relative change in log-likelihood falls below rtol. All estimates are kept within [1e-5, 1 - 1e-5], as in ADMIXTURE. The log of each run (element log of the result) reports the log-likelihood at each iteration, together with that of the quasi-Newton point ("QN") and that of the plain block updates ("basic"). The latter is only computed when the quasi-Newton point is rejected (otherwise it is reported as "not computed"), which saves a pass over the genotypes in most iterations.

A few numerical safeguards handle degenerate cases, without changing the results when the computations are well behaved: for example, a Newton step that is not finite (because a genotype is impossible under the current estimates) is discarded, and the individual or locus keeps its current value for that iteration.

Genotype likelihoods

With genotype likelihoods, the genotypes are not observed: each individual has the likelihoods of its data (its reads) given each of the three genotypes at a locus, with 0, 1 and 2 copies of allele2. tidygenclust does not store them: a package that does can provide a method of gt_radmix_data() for its class. The model is that of NGSadmix (Skotte et al. 2013): the genotypes follow the ADMIXTURE model, with P the frequency of allele2, and the log-likelihood is $$\sum_{ij} \log \sum_{g=0}^{2} P(D_{ij} | g) P(g | x_{ij}),$$ where \(x_{ij} = \sum_k q_{ik} p_{kj}\), \(P(g | x)\) is binomial (Hardy-Weinberg proportions), and the likelihoods \(P(D_{ij} | g)\) of each individual are normalised to sum to 1, as in the beagle files read by NGSadmix. Individuals without data at a locus do not contribute to it, whereas NGSadmix counts \(\log(1/3)\) for each of them (they have three equal likelihoods): otherwise, the log-likelihoods of the two programs are the same.

The algorithm is the same as for genotypes: every step uses the expected numbers of copies of each allele given the likelihoods and the current estimates in place of the observed ones. EM steps are then those of NGSadmix, and the gradients of the block updates are exact; as the log-likelihood of genotype likelihoods is not concave in each block, the Newton steps use the curvature of the expected log-likelihood of the genotypes (that of the EM algorithm), which keeps every quadratic program convex. The quasi-Newton steps are accepted on the log-likelihood above. Cross-validation (crossval) is available (see "Cross-validation"), and so are starts from the SVD (init = "svd"): the SVD is then that of the posterior dosages of the genotypes (their expected numbers of copies of allele2) under Hardy-Weinberg proportions with the allele frequencies estimated from the likelihoods (emMAF, Kim et al. 2011), as in the first step of PCAngsd (Meisner and Albrechtsen 2018), computed by a randomised SVD (Halko et al. 2011) whose products are passes over the likelihoods; individuals without data at a locus get the mean dosage. use_imputed is not available for genotype likelihoods. Unlike NGSadmix, which by default drops loci with a minor allele frequency below 0.05 (its option -minMaf), gt_radmix() uses all the loci of x: select them beforehand if needed.

Supervised analyses

As with ADMIXTURE's --supervised option, the ancestry of some individuals can be given rather than estimated: supervised gives the population of each of these reference individuals (and NA for the individuals to estimate), and each population is one of the k ancestral populations, so k must equal the number of populations in supervised. The ancestry proportions of each reference individual are fixed at 1 for its population and 0 for the others (moved inside the feasible set like every estimate, i.e. 1 - (k - 1) 1e-5 and 1e-5, as reported by ADMIXTURE); the allele frequencies of the ancestral populations (P) are estimated from all the individuals, and the ancestry of the other individuals is estimated given them. Each column of Q and P is one reference population: in the order of the levels of supervised if it is a factor, or of their first appearance otherwise (the order used by ADMIXTURE for the populations of its .pop file). The populations are listed in the element ref_pops of the result (the columns of Q keep the names .Q1, .Q2, ..., which tidypopgen's methods expect).

The fit is the same as in an unsupervised analysis (random start, EM priming, block updates and quasi-Newton steps), with the reference individuals fixed from the start; their ancestry proportions are never updated, and the passes over the genotypes skip the work that only serves them, so a supervised fit with many reference individuals is faster than an unsupervised one. Cross-validation (crossval = TRUE) is available, as in ADMIXTURE: the reference individuals stay fixed in the fit of each fold, and their genotypes belong to the folds and are predicted like the others (ADMIXTURE does not document this detail). init_q (whose rows for the reference individuals are ignored) and init_p can give starting values; fix_q, fix_p and init = "svd" cannot be combined with supervised. Supervised analyses are also available for genotype likelihoods.

When the reference individuals are many, starting P from the allele frequencies of the reference populations, as fastmixture does in its supervised mode, can save iterations: pass them as init_p (the frequency of the alternate allele, e.g. from tidypopgen::loci_alt_freq() on the individuals of each population, in the order of the columns), with n_em_iter = 0 (the individuals to estimate then start from random values). On the HGDP data (K = 5, 660 of 1043 individuals as references), this took 7 iterations instead of 11 and 5 EM steps, to the same log-likelihood; with fewer references (EUR_subset, 102 of 379), it made no difference.

Starting values from the SVD

With init = "svd", each run starts from the principal components of the genotypes rather than from random values, as in ADAMIXTURE (Saurina-i-Ricos et al. 2026) and fastmixture (Santander et al. 2024):

  1. a partial SVD of the genotypes, centred and scaled as by tidypopgen::gt_pca_partialSVD(), with max(k) + 5 components, is computed once and shared by all the runs (monomorphic loci, which the default scaling of tidypopgen rejects, are left unscaled);

  2. for each run, alternating least squares (ALS) find Q and P whose product approximates the allele frequencies predicted by the first k + 5 components, starting from random allele frequencies. As in ADAMIXTURE, the least squares are bounded, the loci are weighted by the inverse of their binomial variance when solving for Q, and Q is extrapolated (momentum) when solving for P. The ALS only uses the SVD, not the genotypes, so it is fast;

  3. the best of 3 such solutions, by log-likelihood, starts the fit, without EM priming (n_em_iter is not used).

The SVD cannot use missing genotypes, so they must be imputed first (e.g. with tidypopgen::gt_impute_simple()); the imputed genotypes are only used for the SVD, and the fit ignores them (unless use_imputed = TRUE). The SVD also needs more individuals and loci than max(k) + 5. With genotype likelihoods, the SVD is that of the posterior dosages (see "Genotype likelihoods"), and needs no imputation; its random test matrix is drawn after setting the first value of seed, and its number of power iterations is svd_power (3 by default, enough for the leading components, those of the structure; each further iteration makes the trailing components more accurate at the cost of two more passes over the likelihoods).

Fits from the SVD need fewer iterations (often less than half as many as from random starts in our tests), and usually reach a good fit (though, as from any start, not always the best one). They are therefore useful for a single good fit of a large dataset, where many random runs would be costly, or as a first exploration before a more extensive search with random starts. However, the starts of different runs vary little, and favour some solutions over others: to explore the modes of the likelihood with several runs (e.g. with gt_clumppling()), use random starts (the default), and do not mix runs started in the two ways, as the runs started from the SVD would over-represent the solutions that they favour.

Cross-validation

With crossval = TRUE, the cross-validation error of ADMIXTURE (Alexander and Lange 2011) is computed for each run, and can be used to choose k (lower is better; see autoplot(type = "cv")). The observed genotypes are split into n_folds folds of roughly equal size; for each fold, the model is refitted with the genotypes of that fold treated as missing, and each of them is predicted by its expected value \(\mu = n \sum_k q_{ik} p_{kj}\), where \(n\) is the number of allele copies of the individual. The error is the binomial deviance $$d(g, \mu) = g \log(g / \mu) + (n - g) \log((n - g) / (n - \mu))$$ averaged over all the masked genotypes of all folds. Where ADMIXTURE does not document the details, we made the following choices:

  • each fold is fitted starting from the estimates for the full data, with at most max_iter iterations and a convergence threshold of 1e-7 (or rtol, if larger) by default (see below for cv_max_iter and cv_rtol);

  • genotypes are assigned to folds by a hash of their position and of a seed drawn from the random number generator (reproducible with seed), so the folds differ from those of ADMIXTURE and the errors agree with ADMIXTURE's closely but not exactly;

  • pseudohaploid individuals use \(n = 1\).

With genotype likelihoods, the folds are drawn over the individuals and loci with data, in the same way, and the error of a masked individual and locus is the deviance of its likelihoods, $$d = \log \max_x f(x) - \log f(x_{ij}),$$ where \(f(x) = \sum_{g} P(D_{ij} | g) P(g | x)\) is the likelihood of its data given a frequency \(x\) of allele2 (see "Genotype likelihoods"), maximised over \(x\) in \([0, 1]\), and \(x_{ij}\) is the prediction of the refitted model. For the likelihoods of a hard call, this is the binomial deviance above (with \(n = 2\)); with uncertain genotypes, the errors are smaller, as the data say less about each genotype, so they can be compared across values of k but not with those of genotypes.

Cross-validation does not change the estimates of Q and P, but requires n_folds additional fits for each run (each usually converging in a few iterations).

The refits of the folds stop earlier than the fit to the full data (cv_rtol = 1e-7, against rtol = 1e-8), and can be shortened further with cv_max_iter (at most that many iterations per fold; ADAMIXTURE refits each fold with 5) or a larger cv_rtol. This saves time, but biases the errors downwards: each refit starts from the estimates for the full data, which have seen the masked genotypes, and a refit stopped early still predicts them too well, the more so at larger k. In our tests, the default halved the cost of cross-validation on EUR_subset (379 individuals, 54,051 loci, k = 1-6, 5 seeds), where refits run to rtol took 24 iterations on average, and lowered the errors by at most 1.5e-5 up to k = 4, and by 1.2e-4 and 2e-4 at k = 5 and 6, while the errors of successive values of k differed by 5e-4 to 3e-3. On the HGDP (1,043 individuals, 130,943 loci, k = 2-10, 3 seeds), where refits converge in about 7 iterations, it saved 11% of the passes and changed the errors by less than 1e-6. Shorter refits save more on EUR_subset (cv_rtol = 1e-6: 74%; cv_max_iter = 5: 80%) with larger biases (up to 6.7e-4 and 1e-3 at k = 6). None of these choices changed the value of k with the lowest error, for any seed. To refit each fold to convergence, set cv_rtol = rtol.

Reproducibility

The random starting values (and the folds of cross-validation) are drawn from R's random number generator, so runs are reproducible with seed (or set.seed()). The work is divided between threads in a way that depends only on the dimensions of the data, so the results are identical for any n_cores.

On x86-64 Linux, when the package is compiled with GCC 12 or later, the main computations are also compiled for processors with the AVX2 and FMA instructions (most processors made since 2015), and the faster version is chosen when the package is loaded. Results are reproducible on a given machine, but can differ in the last digits between machines with and without these instructions. Compiling the package with -DRADMIX_NO_MULTIVERSION (e.g. added to CXXFLAGS in ~/.R/Makevars) builds only the portable version, whose results are the same on every x86-64 machine.

Comparison with ADMIXTURE

The model, the log-likelihood and the optimisation strategy are those of ADMIXTURE (Alexander et al. 2009; Alexander and Lange 2011), so both programs reach the same maximum likelihood estimates, up to local optima and the convergence criterion (ADMIXTURE stops when the log-likelihood increases by less than 1e-4 between iterations). The test suite checks this on the EUR_subset data of SnpArrays.jl. Note that:

  • ADMIXTURE reports the frequency of the second allele in the PLINK bim file, which for a gen_tibble is the reference allele, so its P matrices are 1 - P of those returned here;

  • cross-validation follows ADMIXTURE (see above), and the test suite checks that the errors agree with those of ADMIXTURE on EUR_subset;

  • ADMIXTURE treats the autosomal genotypes of every individual as diploid, whereas gt_radmix() counts a single allele per locus for pseudohaploid individuals (see above);

  • supervised analyses (supervised) follow ADMIXTURE's --supervised option: the same fixed ancestry of the reference individuals, the same order of the populations, and the same requirement that k equals their number; supervised gives the populations as a vector (with NA for the individuals to estimate) instead of a .pop file (with -). The test suite checks the estimates against those of ADMIXTURE on EUR_subset;

  • bootstrap standard errors, available in ADMIXTURE, are not implemented.

Examples

bed_file <-
  system.file("extdata", "pop_a.bed", package = "tidypopgen")
pop_a <- tidypopgen::gen_tibble(bed_file,
  backingfile = tempfile("pop_a"),
  quiet = TRUE
)
adm <- gt_radmix(pop_a, k = 2, seed = 1)
adm$Q[[1]]
#>            .Q1       .Q2
#> [1,] 0.5051543 0.4948457
#> [2,] 0.0000100 0.9999900
#> [3,] 0.9999900 0.0000100
#> [4,] 0.0000100 0.9999900
#> [5,] 0.9999900 0.0000100
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "q_matrix" "matrix"   "array"   

# choose k by cross-validation
adm_cv <- gt_radmix(pop_a, k = 1:3, seed = 1, crossval = TRUE)
adm_cv$cv
#> [1] 0.8224648 1.1840311 0.7096221

# supervised analysis: the first two individuals are references of
# population "A" and the next two of population "B"; the ancestry of the
# others is estimated
pops <- rep(NA, nrow(pop_a))
pops[1:4] <- c("A", "A", "B", "B")
adm_sup <- gt_radmix(pop_a, k = 2, seed = 1, supervised = pops)
adm_sup$ref_pops
#> [1] "A" "B"
adm_sup$Q[[1]]
#>          .Q1     .Q2
#> [1,] 0.99999 0.00001
#> [2,] 0.99999 0.00001
#> [3,] 0.00001 0.99999
#> [4,] 0.00001 0.99999
#> [5,] 0.00001 0.99999
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "q_matrix" "matrix"   "array"
